subject: Adaptive module consolidation — questions on downgrade protection and credits
messages:
From: Sarah Monroe <sarah@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0500
Subject: Adaptive module consolidation inquiry — downgrade/credit questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We dug into the internal billing and product teams and have one strategic ask: we want to consolidate our three current subscriptions (Edge, Throughput, and Features) into a single "adaptive module" that automatically shifts capacity between throughput and feature entitlements. The goal is to simplify finance reporting and reduce manual reassignments when usage patterns spike.

Before we proceed we'd like clarity on a couple of important packaging items:

- Downgrade protection: if we consolidate and then need to step down capacity inside the first year, what's Redwood's approach to preserving feature entitlements vs. throughput tokens? Is there a swapback window?
- Credit handling: will unused throughput in month N be converted into feature credits or lost? Any caps?
- Pricing guardrails: we expect a 12-month commitment but want an introductory blended rate for year one. How do you typically model that?
- Attachments: sending our current TierMap for visibility (Clearline_MAL_TierMap.pdf).

Tom and I are flexible for a short call — ideally next week. Also fine to get a one-page proposal if that's faster.

Best,
Sarah Monroe
Head of Platform Operations
Clearline Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Adaptive module consolidation inquiry — downgrade/credit questions

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks for the clear overview and for sending the TierMap. I reviewed it with our product and finance partners; attaching a quick model that shows a few consolidation approaches (Adaptive_Consolidation_Calc.xlsx).

Short answers up front:
- Swapback window: we can offer a 60-day swapback window for the initial 12-month commitment (allows you to revert allocations between throughput and feature buckets without penalty). After that window we recommend a cadence-based reallocation (quarterly).
- Unused throughput: we propose a capped conversion that preserves up to 20% of average monthly throughput as feature credits for the following month — anything beyond that would be lost (this prevents credit banking abuse and keeps unit economics intact).
- Intro blended pricing: we can structure a Year‑1 blended rate with a 15% introductory concession tied to a 12‑month commit and a minimum committed throughput lane.

I want to loop Ben (solutions) and David (rev ops) to finalize the mechanics and impact to invoicing. Ben/David — can you review the calc and confirm whether the 60-day swapback + 20% capped conversion is workable from engineering and finance perspectives?

If agreeable, I can send a concise one‑page term summary for signoff and lock the model into CL-4721. Also here’s a calendar link: https://cal.com/evelyn/30m

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Adaptive module consolidation inquiry — internal note

Eve / David — quick internal notes after skimming the TierMap + calc:

- Engineering constraints: routing between throughput lanes and "feature entitlements" is doable but has complexity when customers are on Dedicated capacity. If Clearline runs on shared hosted, the KV/prefix cache conversion is straightforward; for Dedicated we need to guarantee reserved slots (so swapbacks eat into reserved utilization).
- Proposed packaging behavior (recommended):
  * 60-day swapback window (as you proposed).
  * 20% capped conversion of throughput to feature credits per rolling month.
  * Grace-tier: allow one emergency one-time swap per year beyond the cap (manual approval).

- Discounting: we can support a 15% blended intro concession for Y1, but finance will want a minimum committed throughput (e.g., 2M tokens/mo) or a stepdown floor. We should avoid open-ended credits on top of large percent discounts.

- Billing mechanics (David input): prefer to create a credit reserve line on the invoice rather than proration against usage — that makes refunds/rollovers auditable. If Clearline insists on proration, there will be a longer accounting review.

Happy to demo the allocation flow in the console for Sarah/Tom.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Tom — following up with a concise proposal based on our internal review. I’ve attached the modeling file and summarized the commercial terms below so you can share with finance/product. If this looks good we’ll convert into a one-page MOU and then a subscription amendment.

Proposed summary (high level):
- Structure: single Adaptive Module consolidating Edge/Throughput/Features. Monthly reporting separates usage by logical "lanes" but invoices as one line item.
- Swapback window: 60 days from go‑live. Allows reallocation between throughput and feature lanes without penalty.
- Credits: capped conversion of unused throughput to feature credits = up to 20% of the trailing 3-month average monthly throughput. One emergency swap allowed per 12 months (manual approval).
- Discounting: Year‑1 blended concession = 15% off list, conditioned on a 12‑month commitment and a minimum committed throughput of 2,000,000 tokens/month.
- Billing: Redwood will create a credit reserve line for converted credits (auditable on each invoice). Proration only by exception (requires finance signoff).
- Next steps: 
  1) Review attached model (Adaptive_Consolidation_Calc.xlsx).
  2) Confirm interest in 15% intro concession and minimum throughput floor.
  3) If confirmed, we’ll generate a 1‑page MOU and schedule a 30‑minute signoff call.

Attachment: Adaptive_Consolidation_Calc.xlsx
